payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly render its content in a pencil-drawn style?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image is clearly rendered as a pencil drawing while representing the image’s visual content. Fail if it is clearly not rendered as a pencil drawing. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the style cannot be determined.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image against the requested pencil-drawing outcome; do not require a source-to-edit progress check.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image preserves the meal and surrounding objects, rendered in muted grayscale with visible pencil-like shading and sketch texture.

fulfillment: The trace’s “yes” is not supported by the rubric: the edit clearly makes substantial progress toward a pencil drawing (muted, near-grayscale palette and visible sketch-like texture) while retaining the scene, but the result still has conspicuous residual color and does not read consistently as a completed pencil drawing. This is visual evidence for partial fulfillment, not a transport or schema failure. The node’s binding is broadly appropriate; repair its decision criterion so a positive endpoint requires the requested style to be convincingly achieved across the image, rather than treating any pencil-like shading or texture as sufficient. Preserve the separate progress check and the rule that unrelated edits do not count. Also avoid treating a conditionally skipped support as evidence: the current trace explicitly skips s2 after s1 passes, so it cannot establish partial progress or independently validate completion. Ensure the endpoint logic can distinguish incomplete-but-relevant style progress from full completion, and returns unknown when the necessary visual observations are unavailable. The high-confidence pass despite visible residual color suggests the criterion is too permissive, not that confidence or repeated variation alone proves the edit absent.

Keep progress assessment separate so relevant but incomplete styling can yield partial rather than no progress, and return unknown when visual evidence is unavailable or indeterminate. This is a semantic criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure; confidence alone does not resolve the visible mismatch."}
